title: Adaptive mesh-based KV allocation and live reshuffle
creator: Aisha Cole
description:
Goal: reduce long-term KV cache fragmentation without regressing tail latency for continuous-batching workloads. We propose an adaptive mesh allocator that splits the GPU KV pool into logical mesh cells (variable-sized bins driven by recent token-length and KV footprint histograms) and a low-impact live reshuffle/compaction pipeline that runs opportunistically during idle GPU epochs. The design trades off immediate free-list compaction costs for sustained utilization gains and fewer full-evictions during high-load bursts.

Key ideas: 1) Mesh cells are size classes derived from empirical batch sequence-length histograms; we maintain hot/cold markers per cell and allow short-lived oversubscription in hot cells with soft quotas. 2) Allocations get a lightweight generation tag so the background reshuffle can move whole generations between cells with double-buffered indirection (no stop-the-world). 3) Compaction triggers: cell fragmentation > 28% or sustained tail eviction rate increase for 10s. 4) Eviction policy integrates recency, generation-staleness, and compactability score (prefer evicting items that will yield contiguous free regions). 5) Continuous-batching awareness: when forming batches we try to align batch KV references to mesh cell boundaries to reduce cross-cell scattering; batching paths can annotate requests with expected token horizon to inform allocation behavior.

Implementation notes: use a per-GPU background compactor worker pinned to a low-priority SM thread group for memcpy scheduling; prioritize device-to-device copies for in-GPU migration and fall back to host staging only when unavoidable. Keep metadata (indirection table, per-cell free-run histograms) in pinned host memory for quick read/writes by control-plane threads. Telemetry: emit kv_mesh_utilization_pct, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_compaction_time_ms, avg_eviction_latency_ms, batch_kv_scatter_pct.

Trade-offs and risks: background compaction increases GPU bandwidth; we limit compaction concurrency and backoff when throughput or tail latency increases. Double-buffered indirection increases memory overhead (~1.2% of KV index), but avoids pinning pages. The adaptive mesh approach may need tuning across model families; we'll provide an automated heatmap-to-bin tool to generate initial mesh configs per model family.

Success metrics: fragmentation ratio < 18% in steady state for common RLHF prompt distributions; 10-25% reduction in full-eviction events during 95th-percentile burst windows; no more than 2% regression in 99th-token latency during canary runs.

Rollout plan: dev cluster -> metric dry-run with compactor disabled (emit telemetry only) -> canary (10 GPUs) with compactor low concurrency -> fleet ramp if metrics stable -> enable for dedicated capacity customers opt-in.
